title: Grothendieck–Lefschetz formula over a finite ring
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum
$p,a,q,k_0,k$, where $q=p^a$, and the
coefficient conventions,
$A=A_{E,n}$. Let $X_0$ be a
separated finite-type
$k_0$-scheme, put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, let
$(K,\varphi)\in D^b_{ctf,\mathrm W}(X,A)$ be a
strict Weil complex whose
underlying $K$ has an
explicit etale-origin
witness, and assume
the exceptional-adjoint admissibility
hypotheses of [def-trf-admissibility] for the structure morphism
and the fixed-point base changes, including those on a chosen
compactification
defined over $k_0$. For every integer $m\geq1$,

$$
\boxed{
\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(F_{c,K}^{\,m}\mid R\Gamma_c(X,K)\bigr)
=
\sum_{y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})}
\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(F_{y,m}\mid K_{\bar y}\bigr).}
$$

Equivalently, in the closed-point form,

$$
\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(F_{c,K}^{\,m}\mid R\Gamma_c(X,K)\bigr)
=
\sum_{\substack{x\in|X_0|\\
d_x\mid m}}
d_x\,\operatorname{tr}_A
\bigl(F_x^{\,m/d_x}\mid K_{\bar x}\bigr).
$$

Both sides lie in $A$, and both sums are finite.

proof.text: Use the braided-monoidal trace of [sk-d-trace], specialized to perfect $A$-complexes by [def-trf-categorical-trace]: for any perfect $A$-complex $P$ and endomorphism $v$, its defining evaluation/coevaluation composite is an element of $\operatorname{End}_{D(A)}(A[0])\cong A$. In Step 5 the coefficient-morphism theorem explicitly supplies that the global and stalk endomorphisms are endomorphisms of perfect complexes under the hypotheses verified there. Thus this is the trace convention for the whole argument; a trace on a possibly nonprojective cohomology module is never substituted for it.

source.place: paragraph 1: the coefficient-morphism trace formula; its perfect-complex trace convention

proof.text:
Take $\psi=u_1=\varphi\circ\kappa_K:L\Phi^*K\to K$. The example in [def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism] applies to this strict Weil pair, so $\psi$ is a Frobenius coefficient morphism. Here is the equality of its recursive iterates with the maps of [def-trf-iterated-weil-map]. The base case is $\psi_1=u_1$. If $m>1$ and $\psi_{m-1}=\varphi^{[m-1]}\circ\kappa^{(m-1)}_K$, expand the recursive definition to obtain
$$\psi_m=\varphi\circ\kappa_K\circ L\Phi^*(\varphi^{[m-1]})\circ L\Phi^*(\kappa^{(m-1)}_K).$$
Naturality of $\kappa$ in [prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison] rewrites the two middle arrows as $Lg_\gamma^*(\varphi^{[m-1]})\circ\kappa_{Lg_\gamma^{(m-1)*}K}$. The cocycle law of [lem-trf-iterated-weil-cocycle] identifies $\varphi\circ Lg_\gamma^*(\varphi^{[m-1]})$ with $\varphi^{[m]}$; multiplicativity of the comparison identifies $\kappa_{Lg_\gamma^{(m-1)*}K}\circ L\Phi^*(\kappa^{(m-1)}_K)$ with $\kappa^{(m)}_K$, after the canonical pullback composition identifications. Therefore $\psi_m=\varphi^{[m]}\circ\kappa^{(m)}_K=u_m$, completing induction.

source.place: paragraph 2, first two sentences: the coefficient morphism and equality of iterates

proof.text: For each $m\geq1$, [def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism] defines $F_{c,m}(\psi)=T_{c_m}(\psi_m)$ with $c_m=(\operatorname{id}_X,\Phi^m)$. Step 2 changes this to $T_{c_m}(u_m)$. The strict-Weil assertion of [prop-trf-graph-frobenius-operator], applied to the given $(K,\varphi)$ and this positive integer $m$, gives $T_{c_m}(u_m)=F_{c,K}^{\,m}$. This identifies the global operators as endomorphisms of the same compact-support complex.

Let $y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$. By [thm-trf-frobenius-fixed-points] its geometric lift $\bar y:s=\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ satisfies $\Phi^m\bar y=\bar y$. Write $M=\operatorname{For}(K,\varphi)$ and $S_y(N)=\operatorname{Fib}_s(L\bar y^*N)$ for the ordinary coefficient-complex stalk functor specified by [def-trf-frobenius-operators]; thus $K_{\bar y}=S_y(M)$. Let $b_y=\rho_{y,m}:S_y(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}S_y(L\Phi^{m*}M)$ be that definition's pullback identification for the fixed-point equality. Using the specified comparison of [prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison], the operator definition gives
$$\tau_{y,m}=S_y(\kappa^{(m)}_M)\circ b_y,\qquad F_{y,m}=S_y(\varphi^{[m]})\circ\tau_{y,m}.$$
The stalk endomorphism in the coefficient-morphism formula is obtained by precomposing the stalk of $\psi_m$ with this same $b_y$. Apply the functor $S_y$ to Step 2 and use preservation of composition to obtain
$$\psi_{m,\bar y}=S_y(u_m)\circ b_y=S_y(\varphi^{[m]})\circ S_y(\kappa^{(m)}_M)\circ b_y=S_y(\varphi^{[m]})\circ\tau_{y,m}=F_{y,m}.$$
All terms here are morphisms of ordinary $A$-complexes, with the same source and target $K_{\bar y}$.

source.place: paragraph 2: fixed points and the stalk transport induced by kappa^(m)

proof.text:
Apply [thm-trf-coefficient-morphism-trace-formula] to the given $X_0$, $K$ and the coefficient morphism $\psi$ of Step 2. Its field datum and ring $A=A_{E,n}$ are unchanged. Its separated finite-type and finite-Tor constructibility hypotheses, explicit étale-origin witness, and the exceptional admissibility requirements on the graphs and fixed-point base changes on the chosen $k_0$-compactification are precisely those assumed in the item; its statement does not require an invertible coefficient map. It gives
$$\operatorname{tr}_A(F_{c,m}(\psi)\mid R\Gamma_c(X,K))=\sum_{y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})}\operatorname{tr}_A(\psi_{m,\bar y}\mid K_{\bar y}).$$
Substituting the endomorphism equalities of Steps 3 and 4 gives the boxed rational-point formula. The cited theorem carries the unit's finite-scheme, affine-line, affine-induction and localization argument, so this specialization keeps that route.

source.place: paragraph 1 and paragraph 2: substitute psi=u_1 into the coefficient-morphism formula

proof.text:
Group the rational-point sum by the underlying closed point $x$. For completeness a rational point has closed image: on an affine neighborhood its coordinate homomorphism has image a finite integral domain in $\mathbf F_{q^m}$, hence a field; any specialization lies in an affine neighborhood also containing the original point, where its prime is maximal. Its residue field is thus a subfield of $\mathbf F_{q^m}$, and the degree tower gives $d_x\mid m$. Conversely [lem-trf-local-frobenius-conjugacy](1) gives exactly $d_x$ geometric lifts over a degree-$d_x$ closed point; when $d_x\mid m$ all these lifts are fixed by $\Phi^m$. The fixed-point identification of [thm-trf-frobenius-fixed-points] makes them exactly the $d_x$ rational points above $x$. Choose one lift over $\mathbf F_{q^{d_x}}$ and let $F_x$ be its one-circuit operator. For every rational point $y$ above $x$, [lem-trf-frobenius-degree-formula] gives
$$\operatorname{tr}_A(F_{y,m}\mid K_{\bar y})=\operatorname{tr}_A(F_x^{m/d_x}\mid K_{\bar x}).$$
Thus the entire group contributes $d_x$ times this element of $A$. The conjugacy assertion of [lem-trf-local-frobenius-conjugacy](3) makes the one-circuit conjugacy class independent of the chosen lift. Summing the groups gives exactly the asserted closed-point formula; the integer $d_x$ acts by repeated addition in $A$.

source.place: paragraph 2, last sentence: group rational points by closed points

proof.text: The fixed-scheme isomorphism of [thm-trf-frobenius-fixed-points] has finite left side and one disjoint $\operatorname{Spec}k$ component for each member of $X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$. Hence this rational-point set is finite. Step 6 partitions it into the nonempty groups of size $d_x$ indexed by $d_x\mid m$, so the closed-point sum also has a finite index set. The two expressions are equal by this finite regrouping, and all summands and the global trace lie in $A$ by the trace convention in Step 1 and the perfectness supplied in Step 5. This proves the finiteness and value assertions as well as both displayed identities.

source.place: paragraph 2, final grouping argument: finiteness of both sums

proof_origin.place: both proof paragraphs, with the iterate induction, specified stalk transport and finite regrouping expanded
